name: Diagnostic imaging & radiology (category guide)
summary: MRI / CT / X-ray / ultrasound cash vs referral — foreigner fee honesty, insurer pre-auth traps, and why a wellness scan is not a specialist work-up.
body: Expats hit imaging in two modes: GP- or specialist-ordered diagnostics for a complaint, and cash ‘full body’ MRI/CT packages marketed as peace of mind. Foreigners pay unsubsidised rates in public hospitals; private centres sell speed and evening slots, not MOH co-funding. Most group outpatient riders reimburse imaging only with a panel referral and often need pre-authorisation above a dollar threshold — arriving cash-pay then claiming later is a common reject. Wellness MRI buffet packages rarely replace a targeted specialist order (ENT tinnitus MRI vs executive whole-body theatre). Ask who reports the study (radiologist name), how incidental findings are handed off, and whether contrast / sedation is quoted separately. Pair with the health-screening category guide when you are shopping packages, and with physio / ENT paths when imaging is part of a work-up. This is a category guide, not a ranked imaging-centre list.
